Title: Econpile wins RM73mil Hospital Tung Shin project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Econpile Holdings Bhd's (Econpile) wholly owned subsidiary, Econpile (M) Sdn Bhd, secured a RM73 million contract from SA Architects Sdn Bhd, on behalf of Hospital Tung Shin, for piling and foundation works for the construction of a new hospital building in Jalan Pudu.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the company said the scope of work includes earth retaining structures, piling, pile cap works and the lowest basement slab for the proposed construction of a new hospital.
"The new hospital building comprises two basement levels, three lower-ground levels of hospital facilities, five levels of car parks, six upper levels of hospital facilities, two office levels and a rooftop mechanical level," it said.
Econpile said the project has a 21-month duration, starting from Nov 1, 2026.
"The project is expected to contribute positively to the revenue and earnings of the company from the financial year ending June 30, 2027 onwards," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dialog to expand Tanjung Langsat storage capacity by 100,000 cubic metres
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd is undertaking a new expansion phase at its Tanjung Langsat terminals in Johor with an additional 100,000 cubic metres of storage capacity for petroleum products.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the integrated technical services provider said the expansion is expected to commence immediately.
Its expected completion by mid-2029 would bring its total combined storage capacity in Tanjung Langsat to more than 1.1 million cubic metres.
It said the expansion will involve its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Dialog Terminals Langsat (3) Sdn Bhd (DTL3).
"Dialog will undertake the engineering, procurement and construction (EPCC) of the storage facilities for petroleum and petrochemical-related products connected to existing marine facilities," it said.
The additional space is expected to contribute positively to the company's future earnings.
"The company will remain focused on diversifying its operations across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sectors, as well as the sustainable and renewable energy sectors.
"The strategy will position the company to participate in, and benefit from, different economic and oil price cycles, in line with its objective of generating long-term recurring income," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas Gas completes transfer of gas processing, utilities businesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Gas Bhd (PGB) has completed the transfer of its gas processing and utilities businesses to two subsidiaries under the proposed internal reorganisation effective Nov 1, 2026.
In a filing to Bursa Malaysia today, PGB said its gas processing business was transferred to PG Gas Processing Sdn Bhd while the utilities business was transferred to PG Utilities East Sdn Bhd following the fulfilment of the conditions precedent under the respective business transfer agreements (BTAs).
"In this regard, certain conditions precedent relating to the receipt of approvals from the relevant authorities and the issuance of new licences and approvals have been waived in accordance with the respective BTAs," it added.
PGB noted that PG Gas Processing and PG Utilities East commenced their respective operations with effect from Nov 1.
"The transfer and/or vesting of the gas transportation business to PG TransCo Sdn Bhd pursuant to the proposed internal reorganisation will take place at a later date, subject to the fulfilment of the conditions precedent under the relevant BTA," it added
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bukit Aman to record Rafizi's statement over Ramanan bribery allegation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police will record Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli's statement over claims that PKR vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan received a RM9.5 million bribe in connection with the corporate mafia issue.
The Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) founder said he was scheduled to be at Bukit Aman federal police headquarters at 10am to facilitate investigations under Sections 500 and 505 of the Penal Code for criminal defamation and statements conducing to public mischief.
The offences are punishable by jail terms, fines, or both.
Rafizi is accused of making the statements during a speech in Selayang on Oct 20.
The former Pandan member of parliament said his speech also touched on a court case involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
"What I am going through now is no different from the police investigations and court charges when I exposed the 1MDB, Tabung Haji, Felda and National Feedlot Corporation issues in the past.
"The courts acquitted me in all those cases," he said in a statement, accusing the government of trying to intimidate him.
Rafizi added that he had initiated legal action against Ramanan after the latter did not take the matter to court.
"Ramanan should have taken the same action against me if he truly wanted to clear his name from allegations of taking a RM9.5 million bribe to settle a corporate mafia case.
"I have initiated a lawsuit against him because he refused to go to court over my allegations."
Ramanan, the human resources minister, previously denied Rafizi's claims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly couple killed, son injured in car-bus collision in Gerik
Article:
GERIK: An elderly couple were killed and their son seriously injured when their Perodua Alza collided with a tour bus along the East-West Highway near the Titiwangsa rest area today.
The 64-year-old man and his 58-year-old wife died in the 1.40pm crash along the Gerik-bound stretch, while their 28-year-old son was taken to Gerik Hospital.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said all three victims were trapped in the car following the collision.
"The driver and front-seat passenger were unconscious, while the man in the rear seat was seriously injured.
"Firefighters used rescue equipment to free all three," he said in a statement.
He added that the bus driver, two assistants and all 30 passengers escaped unhurt.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SAG lands RM51.6mil Underwater World Langkawi project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Signature Alliance Group Bhd (SAG) has secured a RM51.56 million contract to redevelop and refurbish Underwater World Langkawi.
The contract was awarded to its subsidiary Zig Zag Builders, through a construction works agreement with Underwater World Langkawi Sdn Bhd, the attraction's owner and operator.
Located in Pantai Cenang, Underwater World Langkawi is part of Main Market-listed Eden Inc Bhd and has been operating since August 1995.
The project is scheduled to begin on Nov 13 and will take 18 months to complete.
It is expected to contribute positively to SAG's earnings and net assets throughout the contract period.
The contract, secured on Nov 2, was not included in the company's previously reported unbilled order book of RM228.6 million as at June 30.
SAG executive director and group chief executive officer Datuk Chang Chung Fei said the contract marked a significant addition to its project portfolio.
"Underwater World Langkawi is a well-known attraction, and we are pleased to be entrusted with its redevelopment and refurbishment.
"Our team has direct experience working in Langkawi through the previous completed project, and that familiarity with the local operating environment and logistics will be useful as we mobilise for this new assignment," he said in a statement.
Zig Zag Builders previously completed a project worth more than RM40 million on the island.
It involved interior fit-out, cabinetry, joinery, built-in furniture and related works for two blocks of serviced apartments at a commercial hotel property.
According to the Langkawi Development Authority, the island recorded about 3.2 million visitor arrivals in 2025, supporting continued investment in its hospitality and tourism infrastructure.
"As we move into our next phase of growth, our priority is to convert new awards into timely project delivery, progress billings and cash flow," he said.
As at June 30, SAG had a net cash position of around RM80.2 million, providing financial flexibility to fund larger projects alongside its planned capacity expansion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zulkifli defends RM15,000 haj savings rule amid TH cash flow allegations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has sought to defend the RM15,000 minimum savings requirement for haj registration.
Zulkifli told the Dewan Rakyat that the decision to introduce the Seruan Istito'ah (capacity or ability to perform haj) requirement was based on studies and feedback from various stakeholders, not solely the ministry's decision.
This comes amid objections from opposition members of parliament, who argued that the amount was too burdensome for prospective pilgrims facing decades-long waits for their turn.
"The RM15,000 was agreed by the Tabung Haji Syariah Advisory Committee and by the National Haj Muzakarah," he said this when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027.
He added that engagement sessions had been held nationwide, while an online study conducted through the Haj School had also received support from depositors.
He said Malaysia's haj quota was limited to 31,600 pilgrims, while registrations exceeded four million.
"The wait approaches 150 years. That is not realistic, so we must have a realistic system," he said.
The minimum savings requirement could help rationalise the waiting list, he said.
He said savings kept in Tabung Haji for 30 to 40 years would grow through dividends, reducing the need for depositors to top up their accounts when haj costs increased.
However, Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa) interjected and said the opposition had never questioned the principle of istito'ah, but disputed how the government was applying it to the haj waiting list.
"The problem is the government is confused in implementing istito'ah.
"Istito'ah to go for haj is one thing, but istito'ah to get a haj turn - why assess it 50 or 30 years before?" he said.
He said the government could require prospective pilgrims to have RM15,000 in savings a year before their turn, but imposing the requirement 30 or 50 years in advance would place an unnecessary burden on them.
Marzuk claimed the real reason for the requirement was a cash flow problem at Tabung Haji, which he alleged arose because the government had not paid the Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) sukuk that matured in May.
"I think the real purpose (of the haj queue requirement) isn't this. I've heard, though I can't disclose it here, it's a cash flow issue involving Tabung Haji," he said.
Zulkifli replied that istito'ah was not only about financial ability.
"It covers safety, health and quota. It must be considered holistically," he said.
"I stress that this condition is not for the rich, but for those who strive to achieve istito'ah in the haj obligation."
Existing depositors have until Dec 31, 2028
to reach RM15,000 in savings
to keep their place in the queue.
From Jan 1, 2029, the queue will be rearranged based on the minimum savings, and Tabung Haji expects the waiting time to fall to about 70 years.
In August, former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli
alleged that the government
had yet to settle a RM12.5 billion financial commitment to Tabung Haji after UJSB's Series 1 sukuk matured on May 29.
He said the government should have repaid the amount in cash or with assets of equivalent value.
Rafizi said only RM965 million had been settled in property, while the remaining RM11.5 billion was replaced with new sukuk maturing in 10 years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former MMC Port group CEO Azman Shah joins Bank Negara board
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Azman Shah Mohd Yusof has joined Bank Negara Malaysia's board as an independent non-executive member effective Nov 1.
He also serves on the central bank's board audit committee, according to Bank Negara's website.
Azman Shah brings broad experience across sectors, having begun his career as a Bank Negara economist.
He later held senior positions at Pengurusan Danaharta Nasional Bhd and served on the Corporate Debt Restructuring Committee.
His leadership roles include group chief executive officer of MMC Port Holdings Bhd and chief executive officer of Northport (Malaysia) Bhd and Integrax Bhd.
He is a director of AREA Real Estate Advisory Sdn Bhd and vice-president of the Malaysian International Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
He holds an economics degree from the London School of Economics and completed an executive programme at Harvard University.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DKU allowed into Negri Sembilan exco case, but not its secretary
Article:
SEREMBAN: The High Court has dismissed an application by Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin to intervene in an originating summons filed by 10 former Negri Sembilan executive council members over the interpretation of the state constitution.
Judge Roz Mawar Rozain ruled that Raja Norazli had no personal interest in the case, as the interest raised belonged to the DKU as an institution.
However, she allowed the DKU itself to intervene and named it the third defendant, with its participation limited to specific issues to be determined later.
Roz Mawar said the DKU's presence was necessary to ensure an effective and comprehensive determination of the case, including questions concerning the "Ruler" raised by the plaintiffs under Article 28(1) of the state constitution.
She agreed with the plaintiffs that the DKU had no role in appointing or revoking the appointments of state executive council members.
The court also recorded an undertaking by the plaintiffs that the proceedings would continue without asking the court to determine the validity of a proclamation dated April 19, 2026, or who holds the office of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
Earlier, lawyer Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun informed the court that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had withdrawn his consent for the appointment of external counsel to represent the state secretary and state government.
Hafarizam said a letter dated Oct 29 to state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal stated that the state government needed to scrutinise the use of public funds on two grounds.
"First, the financial implications arising from engaging external counsel cannot be properly evaluated.
"Second and most importantly, any decision involving significant state government commitments must first be brought before the state executive council for consideration," he said.
Hafarizam said the letter noted that the exco had not convened, meaning the appointment of external counsel and its financial implications could not be deliberated or decided upon.
"Therefore, it is inappropriate for the state government to continue bearing such spending commitments," he said.
Muzalmah said the letter arrived at her office last Friday while she was attending a meeting in Langkawi. She was also informed that counsel for the plaintiffs had filed an additional affidavit that afternoon.
She said she replied on Monday morning, explaining that the issuance of a fiat fell under the purview of the State Legal Adviser's Office and did not require the menteri besar's consent.
"I met with the menteri besar previously regarding the appointment of counsel, and no objection was raised, and fees were not discussed. That issue does not arise now; it is separate from the appointment," she said.
Roz Mawar questioned whether Ismail had issued the letter in his personal capacity or in his official capacity as menteri besar.
The court fixed Nov 16 at 10am to hear preliminary objections.
All parties were directed to file written submissions by Nov 10, with affidavits in reply to be submitted by Nov 13.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malakoff's 'amazing hunt' puts sustainability in play
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd has brought together employees, stakeholders and media representatives for the fourth edition of its Malakoff Amazing Hunt, which highlighted sustainability and environmental responsibility.
Held on Oct 31 at The Saujana Hotel, the event carried the theme 'Powering a Greener Future' and was flagged off by Malakoff chief financial officer Mohd Nazersham Mansor.
The hunt attracted 88 participants across 22 teams, comprising Malakoff employees, stakeholders of Malakoff and Alam Flora Sdn Bhd, mainstream media representatives and social media personalities.
The event provided participants with insights into the businesses and sustainability commitments of Malakoff and Alam Flora, while encouraging them to promote sustainable living to wider communities.
This year's edition also brought together employees from four Malakoff power plants in Johor, Perak and Penang, alongside colleagues from its Kuala Lumpur headquarters, under the company's 'One Plant, One Pride' initiative.
The initiative aims to strengthen collaboration and camaraderie across the organisation by encouraging employees from different locations and business units to work together.
Structured around the three environmental, social and governance (ESG) pillars, the hunt featured challenges covering carbon reduction, waste management, environmental protection, teamwork, ethics and transparency.
Malakoff group chief executive officer Syahrunizam Samsudin said sustainability should extend beyond corporate commitments and become part of everyday practices.
"At Malakoff and Alam Flora, sustainability is more than a corporate aspiration. Whether through clean energy, waste management or environmental stewardship, we want sustainability to be practical, accessible, and embedded into our everyday lives.
"When we use resources wisely, reduce waste, respect different views and make responsible decisions, we are already helping to build a greener and more resilient future," he said in a statement.
He added that ensuring a reliable and affordable energy supply remained central to Malakoff's role, particularly as Malaysia's economic growth and the expansion of data centres and the digital economy drive demand for dependable, round-the-clock electricity.
On the participation of power plant employees, Syahrunizam said the 'One Plant, One Pride' initiative reinforced the importance of organisational unity.
"When our people feel connected to one another and to the company they work for, we are stronger, we perform better and we serve the nation better," he said.
Winners were recognised across three categories: media, stakeholders and 'One Plant, One Pride'.
The top three teams in each category received cash prizes of RM2,000, RM1,600 and RM1,200 respectively.
Team Huntastic Four emerged as champions in the media category, while Perbadanan Putrajaya won the stakeholders category.
Tanjung Bin Energy 1 took the top spot in the 'One Plant, One Pride' category.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ISF Group wins RM83.2mil data centre jobs in PD
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ISF Group Bhd has bagged RM83.2 million worth of contracts for a hyperscale data centre project in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan, marking the largest contract win in the company's history.
The contracts were awarded to its subsidiary Yeo Plumber Sdn Bhd by an established Malaysian-based civil engineering and building construction company
The four contracts cover various piping and infrastructure works for the data centre development.
Three contracts, worth a combined RM73.3 million, involve cold water systems, rainwater harvesting systems, water reticulation and sanitary services.
The remaining contract, valued at RM9.9 million, covers external sewerage infrastructure works.
The projects are scheduled for completion in stages between November 2026 and July 2028.
Following the latest awards, ISF's unbilled order book has increased to RM225.5 million, providing earnings visibility through the financial year ending Dec 31, 2029.
Managing director Jeff Ai Boon Chen said the contract win marked a significant milestone for the company, reflecting its growing capabilities and ability to undertake larger and more complex projects.
"At RM83.2 million, this is the largest contract we have ever secured. This reflects our growing capabilities and the confidence placed in our ability to undertake increasingly large and complex projects.
"It also demonstrates our readiness to compete for projects of a much greater scale," he said in a statement.
Ai said Malaysia's emergence as a regional data centre hub continued to create opportunities for supporting infrastructure works.
With data centres accounting for a significant portion of its business, he said the company was well positioned to secure more projects in the expanding market, supported by its track record in delivering high-specification piping solutions.
He added that the company remained optimistic about its growth prospects, supported by a stronger order book and expanding project portfolio.
Separately, ISF is exploring opportunities to expand into larger-scale water infrastructure projects in Malaysia, particularly water treatment plants and non-revenue water reduction initiatives.
The potential expansion could broaden its project portfolio while complementing its existing piping expertise.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Social media users pay tribute to Boat Noodle, BananaBro founder
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Social media users have paid tribute to Tony Lim, the founder of Boat Noodle and BananaBro, following his death at the age of 47.
Both restaurant brands
announced his passing
in separate Facebook posts earlier today.
"Deepest condolences to the family. Thank you for bringing one of the best banana leaf dishes into my world," said social media user Syamsul Anuar Samsuddin.
Another user, Md Khairul Alam, who worked with Lim, described him as a "genuinely good human being and a wonderful friend".
He also shared a group photo of them dining together.
"As the founder of Boat Noodle and BananaBro, he leaves behind a remarkable legacy and countless memories.
"It was truly a privilege to have worked under his leadership. His kindness, humility, and generosity will always be remembered. He touched many lives and will be deeply missed," he said.
Meanwhile, social media user Julian Vincent praised Lim's legacy, describing it as one built on passion, generosity and a dream of sharing Malaysia's rich banana leaf culture with the world.
He also expressed hope that Lim's contributions would never be forgotten.
Lim made his mark on Malaysia's food and beverage industry in 2014 when he founded Boat Noodle, a Thai street-food concept that introduced small-bowl portions.
Following its success, he launched BananaBro in 2018, bringing a modern approach to traditional banana leaf rice.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wan Fayhsal proposes Shuhaily for corporate mafia task force
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Machang member of parliament (MP) Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has proposed that Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain be appointed to a special inter-agency task force investigating corporate mafia activities.
"I propose, to save government spending, that he be appointed as a member of this special inter-agency task force," he said.
Wan Fayhsal was speaking during the committee-stage debate on the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has asked the attorney-general to
lead the task force.
Wan Fayhsal said Shuhaily who is the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) had extensive experience and was a former Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director.
"Don't throw away good people like this and put them in cold storage at the home ministry," he said.
He said government officers who excelled in fighting corruption should not be victimised.
Shuhaily was charged at the Sepang magistrate's court on Oct 21 with two counts of
assaulting two policemen
at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in September. He pleaded not guilty.
Earlier, the home ministry
decided to return Shuhaily,
who was serving as MCBA director-general on secondment, to the police.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Consumer groups question halal oversight after Puchong slaughterhouse raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Consumer groups have called for clearer enforcement responsibilities and tighter monitoring of halal compliance at slaughterhouses following the seizure of more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken at a Puchong warehouse.
Consumers Association of Kedah (Cake) president Yusrizal Yusuf said overlapping responsibilities among enforcement agencies could create monitoring gaps, allowing violations to go undetected.
He proposed placing halal enforcement under the Islamic Development Department (Jakim), backed by a dedicated law granting the department clear enforcement powers.
"There are four or five laws involved, and everyone passes the responsibility on (to the other party). When something like this happens, who is going to inspect and who is going to take action?
"We hope enforcement can be centralised under one department or agency. We propose Jakim to carry this out," he told the New Straits Times.
He said the agencies involved included the Veterinary Services Department (DVS), the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, health authorities, local councils and Islamic religious departments.
Authorities seized the chicken during a
raid on a Puchong warehouse
on Friday over halal violations.
Following the raid, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari called for stern action, including prosecution, against operators found violating procedures.
He also called for
closer cooperation
between halal certification bodies and local authorities.
Yusrizal backed Amirudin's call but said inspection and enforcement responsibilities needed to be clearly defined to prevent agencies from shifting the responsibility to one another.
He also proposed making halal certification a prerequisite for local authority approval of poultry and cattle slaughterhouses supplying meat to Muslim consumers.
He said monitoring should extend beyond Selangor, as slaughterhouses and poultry suppliers operated nationwide.
Yusrizal urged Jakim to coordinate the requirements with state Islamic religious departments and ensure they maintained records of slaughterhouses in their respective jurisdictions.
"This concerns food for Malaysian Muslims, not just Selangor.
"The religious authorities should have data on these slaughterhouses and could conduct periodic inspections, so we know their level of compliance with standard operating procedures," he said.
Meanwhile, Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) research officer Hatijah Hashim called for the authorities to be scrutinised over possible lapses in slaughterhouse monitoring.
She questioned whether Jakim, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and DVS had fulfilled their oversight responsibilities.
"It is shocking that something like this could happen when so many authorities are involved.
"Strict action should be taken against the slaughterhouse operator responsible for allowing this to happen," she said.
Hatijah added that CAP had repeatedly raised concerns with the authorities over mechanised poultry slaughter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A-GC denies delay in reviewing investigation paper involving Negri MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has denied delaying its review of an investigation paper into Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim's claim that he was forced to sign a proclamation to remove the state ruler.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the police inquiry paper was referred to the A-GC on Sept 29 and returned to the police on Oct 7.
He said police then reclassified the inquiry paper as an investigation paper to allow investigations to be conducted under Section 506 of the Penal Code.
"The investigation paper opened under Section 506 of the Penal Code was only referred to the AGC on Friday (Oct 30) and is now being reviewed by the AGC," he said when contacted.
Dusuki said the AGC maintained that there had been no delay on its part in reviewing the inquiry paper or investigation papers submitted by the police.
The New Straits Times had earlier reported that
Cha Kee Chin (PH-Rasah)
had questioned the A-GC's delay in deciding on the investigation paper concerning Ismail's police report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Handal Energy faces delisting threat
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Handal Energy Bhd faces potential delisting after failing to submit its annual report more than six months after the April 30 deadline.
Bursa Malaysia issued the oil and gas services provider a show-cause notice, requiring it to explain why its securities should not be removed from the exchange.
In a filing on Monday, Handal Energy said it is preparing a written explanation, which must be submitted by Nov 10.
The company has yet to release its annual report and audited financial statements for the financial period ended Dec 31, 2025.
If Bursa decides to delist Handal Energy, its securities will be removed from the exchange within seven market days, unless the company files an appeal within the prescribed timeframe.
Even if Bursa decides against delisting the company, Handal Energy could still face other regulatory action or penalties.
The company has repeatedly delayed releasing its annual report, most recently missing its own target of submitting the report by Oct 28.
The delays have also been compounded by changes to its audit arrangements.
On Oct 20, Handal Energy announced the resignation of its external auditor SBY Partners PLT after the board expressed dissatisfaction with the audit's progress and stated its intention to appoint a replacement.
Previously, the company cited the audit of its 30 per cent-owned subsidiary Tenzin Heavy Machinery (M) Sdn Bhd as a key reason for the delay.
Outstanding matters included cash flow projections, asset impairment assessments and litigation-related liabilities.
Handal Energy has remained in the red, recording losses for 13 consecutive quarters.
For the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, it posted a net loss of RM3.13 million on revenue of just RM53,000.
Its shares have been suspended from trading since May 11 after it missed the original submission deadline.
The stock last traded at one sen, giving the company a market value of about RM4.5 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman rescued from Mini Cooper as heavy rain hits Klang Valley
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman trapped inside a Mini Cooper was rescued by firefighters in Kuala Lumpur following heavy rain, while two other cars were stranded in floodwaters outside a fire station.
The onset of the monsoon season typically brings heavy rain to parts of the country.
The incident was among several reported across the Klang Valley, including a landslide in Shah Alam and a fallen tree that damaged a car in Batu Arang.
The Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 3.30pm and sent six personnel to the scene outside the Pantai Fire and Rescue Station along Jalan Pantai Baharu.
The woman was found safe after being freed from the Mini Cooper.
In Shah Alam, a landslide was reported at a car park near Seri Nilam Apartments along Jalan Sigma U6/14 in Subang Permata.
The landslide affected an area of about 111 sq m, roughly the size of one and a half badminton courts. Six personnel from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station went to the scene to monitor for potential hazards and put up barriers to keep vehicles out.
Meanwhile, a tree fell in front of a house in Bandar Tasik Puteri, Batu Arang, damaging a vehicle.
The Selangor Fire and Rescue Department received a call at 3.39pm and sent six personnel from the Batu Arang Fire and Rescue Station to the scene.
Videos and photographs shared on social media also showed rising water levels in several areas, including Denai Alam, Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI), Bukit Jalil, USJ and the Federal Highway.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Farhash obtains injunction to stop Bloomberg publishing allegedly defamatory report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Farhash Wafa Salvador Rizal Mubarak has obtained a High Court injunction restraining Bloomberg News and its subsidiary from publishing statements he claims to be defamatory.
Judicial commissioner Kan Weng Hin granted the injunction today following legal proceedings initiated by Farhash over an article the news organisation intended to publish.
In a statement today, his lawyers from Messrs Ahmad Deniel, Ruben & Co said the proposed article contained statements and allegations which their client maintained were false, baseless and defamatory.
They said Farhash had received communications from Bloomberg News or its representatives indicating their intention to publish the article before legal proceedings were initiated.
"The court granted an injunction restraining Bloomberg News and all parties from publishing, republishing, circulating or otherwise disseminating the defamatory statements and/or imputations identified in the proceedings.
"This includes statements of a similar nature concerning our client," the firm said.
The lawyers, however, did not disclose the nature of the allegations contained in the proposed article.
Farhash was represented by Aswath Ramakrishnan and Nur Irdina Syahirah Mohammad Wardi.
"As the matter is now before the court, we do not intend to engage in any public debate or litigate the merits of the proceedings through the media.
"Our client remains committed to protecting his reputation and vindicating his rights through the appropriate legal channels," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MARKET PULSE PM NOV 2, 2026 [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed higher as easing crude oil prices helped stabilise investor sentiment following the recent equity sell-off.
The FBM KLCI ended the day 3.91 points higher at 1,619.51.

In the crypto market, Bitcoin rose to RM318,546.
Ethereum and Solana also climbed to RM9,338 and RM383.

Title: #NSTviral: SIA flight's tricky Perth landing attempt draws praise online
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Singapore Airlines (SIA) flight aborted its landing attempt at Perth Airport due to strong winds before landing safely on its second attempt on Oct 31.
A video posted on
Facebook by Chris Perry
showed flight SQ213, travelling from Singapore to Perth, tilting sharply to the right as it approached the runway, with its right wing appearing close to the ground, before climbing away.
Perry, whose sister was on board, said strong winds had forced the aircraft to "go round again", adding that the second landing attempt was successful.
SIA, responding to queries from AsiaOne, confirmed that the aircraft encountered strong winds during its approach, prompting the pilots to perform a go-around.
The airline said the Airbus A350-900 landed safely at 12.30pm local time before taxiing to the gate.
"The safety of our customers and crew is SIA's top priority," it said.
The incident drew praise on social media, with users commending the pilots for handling the difficult approach.
Facebook user Sampath Gur said the incident "must have been pretty frightening for many on board", but praised SIA for being "known for choosing and training the best of the best".
Another user, Sam Howard, said the pilots "held that very well", commending their handling of the situation.
A go-around is a standard aviation safety procedure in which pilots discontinue a landing approach and climb away before making another attempt when conditions are unsuitable.
Perth Airport wind data showed winds of 32kph, with gusts reaching 43kph, around the time the aircraft landed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Caprice ordered to pay Ebit Lew RM220,000 immediately
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Rapper and influencer Caprice has been ordered to pay preacher Ebit Lew RM220,000 in damages immediately after the Sessions Court dismissed his application to stay the payment.
According to Berita Harian, Judge Zuhrina Mohamed Nor ordered Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, 40, to deposit the money into the account of Ebit's lawyers and pay RM2,000 in costs.
Ebit, whose real name is Ebit Irawan Ibrahim Lew, 42, was represented by Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader and Fatin Izyan Mazlan, while Mohd Rezan Ezra Muhammad Mosinal appeared for Caprice.
The court previously ordered
Caprice to apologise
and pay Ebit RM220,000 after finding that he defamed the preacher in 2023.
Caprice was also ordered to remove seven statements made with Indonesian influencer Mondy Tattoo within 48 hours and barred from making further comments or statements about Ebit.
The case stemmed from a video Caprice uploaded on Sept 15, 2023, featuring Mondy as a guest.
Ebit said the video implied he sexually harassed and took advantage of Mondy, and portrayed
him as irresponsible and someone who exploited religion.
He said Caprice, the first defendant, maliciously published the video without first seeking verification from him or his lawyers.
Ebit said the video also drew negative comments, insults and abuse against him from followers of Caprice's YouTube account.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcycle catches fire during refuelling at Machap R&R
Article:
KLUANG: A motorcycle caught fire while being refuelled at a petrol station at the Machap southbound rest and recreation (R&R) area along the North-South Expressway.
The 11.50am incident yesterday was captured on the dashcam of a vehicle parked behind the motorcycle.
The footage, which has since gone viral, showed flames suddenly erupting from the motorcycle as the rider was refuelling. He jumped off, but his shoes caught fire
The motorcycle was soon engulfed in flames, prompting station staff to help put out the fire.
A petrol station employee, who declined to be named, said the rider was unharmed. The motorcycle sustained minor damage, while the exterior of the affected fuel pump was also damaged.
He said the station regularly sent employees for fire safety training conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department.
Signboards around the station remind motorists to switch off their engines and refrain from smoking, vaping or using mobile phones near the pumps.
Motorists are also advised to dismount while refuelling to reduce the risk of injury if fuel spills or catches fire.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police dismantle cross-border scam operations in Penang, arrest 141
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police have arrested 141 people and seized computer equipment worth RM1.4 million after busting online scam syndicates operating across Penang in a series of 14 raids.
The multi-district operation, conducted between Oct 9 and 29, targeted scam call centres operating from luxury condominiums and private residences across three districts.
Five raids were carried out in the northeast district, six in the southwest and three in Seberang Perai Tengah.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the syndicates had used the state as an operational base to target victims overseas.
"Their targets were abroad. They used Malaysia as their operational base to run these scams.
"Penang's prosperity, connectivity, good food, and modern facilities possibly made it an attractive base for them to settle down and conduct their fraudulent operations," Lim told a press conference at the state police headquarters.
The suspects, aged between 18 and 48, comprised nine locals and 132 foreigners consisting of 93 China nationals, 29 Vietnamese, four Japanese, three Taiwanese, two Cambodians, and one from Myanmar.
Lim said the foreign operatives had entered Malaysia legally on tourist passes before misusing their permits to conduct specialised scams targeting victims in specific countries.
They used platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok to carry out their activities.
The operations uncovered several types of scams, including Taiwanese- and Japanese-led call centres involved in phone impersonation and cryptocurrency fraud targeting Japanese victims.
Other syndicates created fake social media accounts or offered bogus customer service jobs to deceive victims in China.
There were also love scam rings targeting victims in Hong Kong and Malaysia, an illegal online gambling operation targeting Brazilians, and a syndicate offering fake fee-recovery services to defraud American scam victims.
Lim said police seized mobile phones, laptops, tablets, internet routers and other computer accessories worth RM1.4 million from the premises.
"Three cases have already been charged in court, while 11 others are under active investigation under Section 420 read together with Section 120B of the Penal Code for cheating, alongside Sections 6(3) and 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TNB taps RM2bil sukuk for Kenyir solar project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) subsidiary has lodged a RM2 billion Islamic medium-term notes facility to finance the development of a hybrid hydro-floating solar project at Kenyir Lake, Terengganu.
The facility, known as the Asean Sustainability SRI Sukuk Wakalah, was lodged with the Securities Commission on Oct 30 by TI TNB Genco Solar Kenyir 1 Sdn Bhd.
TI TNB Genco is 70 per cent-owned by TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of TNB, while the remaining interest is held by Terengganu Incorporated Sdn Bhd through a joint venture arrangement.
The project involves the development of a 595-megawatt (MW) alternating current hybrid hydro-floating solar facility, supported by a 297MW/1,190 megawatt-hour battery energy storage system (BESS).
The facility is being developed under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (Cress), which enables renewable energy supply arrangements between generators and corporate consumers.
"The sukuk shall have a tenure of at least one year and up to 23 years from the date of issuance.
"The issuance of the Asean Sustainability SRI Sukuk Wakalah shall be made no later than 90 business days from the date of lodgement with the Securities Commission or such other extended dates approved," according to TNB's filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
The facility has received a preliminary rating of AA+IS with a stable outlook from MARC Ratings Bhd.
TNB said proceeds from the sukuk would be used to part-finance project development and construction costs, including engineering, procurement, installation, testing and commissioning.
The funds would also be used to reimburse existing shareholders' advances related to project development, finance working capital and pre-operating expenses, as well as meet designated account requirements and facility-related expenses.
All proceeds will be utilised for Shariah-compliant purposes in accordance with the applicable sustainability and responsible investment frameworks.
The sukuk facility is aligned with the SC's Sustainable and Responsible Investment Sukuk Framework, Asean green, social and sustainability bond standards, and the International Capital Market Association's principles and guidelines.
It also falls under TNB's Transition Finance Framework, dated Sept 24, 2024.
The SC's Shariah Advisory Council endorsed the facility on July 6.
RHB Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser and lead arranger, while RHB Investment Bank and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd are the joint lead managers. RHB Islamic Bank Bhd is the Shariah adviser.

Title: JS-SEZ gets ministerial-level boost
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Singapore have upgraded the joint ministerial committee for Iskandar Malaysia (JMCIM) into a ministerial-level platform to strengthen bilateral coordination and accelerate the implementation of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
The new Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) will provide strategic direction and oversee priority initiatives under the economic zone, reflecting the expanding scope of cooperation between the two countries.
"The JSCMC will serve as an enhanced ministerial platform to provide strategic direction, strengthen bilateral coordination and oversee the implementation of priority initiatives under the JS-SEZ," according to a joint statement issued following its inaugural meeting in Singapore today.
The meeting was co-chaired by Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir and Singapore's National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat.
Under the new structure, the joint ministerial committee (JMC) will comprise Malaysia's economy minister, investment, trade and industry minister and Johor Menteri Besar Onn Hafiz Ghazi.
Singapore will be represented by its national development minister, energy, trade and industry minister, and transport minister.
Both countries may also propose additional representatives as required.
The JSCMC will be supported by working groups covering the JS-SEZ, transportation and other areas mutually agreed upon by both countries.
These working groups will report to the JMC, with both sides set to discuss the necessary arrangements to operationalise the structure.
The two countries will also continue discussions on the updated terms of reference for the JSCMC and its working groups ahead of the next meeting, scheduled to be held in Malaysia in 2027.
"The transition of the JMCIM into the JSCMC reflects the deepening and broadening scope of bilateral cooperation," it said.
Both sides also reaffirmed their commitment to establishing the institutional, regulatory and operational frameworks required to support the JS-SEZ.
The inaugural meeting reviewed progress made by the JS-SEZ joint working committee, including infrastructure and utilities development, investment facilitation, cross-border connectivity and talent development collaborations.
Both countries said they were satisfied with the momentum of bilateral cooperation.
"Both sides expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum of bilateral cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to working closely through the JSCMC to drive inclusive growth, strengthen regional competitiveness, and further deepen the longstanding partnership between Singapore and Malaysia," they said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Mayday, mayday': Chilling final cockpit calls before 9 die in Florida jet crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Mayday, mayday" and "We're going to crash into the ground" were among the last words heard from the cockpit of a private jet before it plunged into a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida.
The crash happened on Sunday. All nine people on board the Learjet 60 were killed.
The jet had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the United States Federal Aviation Administration said, according to Reuters.
An air traffic control recording from a Miami control centre, posted on LiveATC and shared by X user @aviationbrk, captured the plane's final moments.
Someone in the cockpit initially told an air traffic controller they were "managing the ice" but were facing "moderate" turbulence and looking for "better rides".
Less than a minute later came the mayday call, with the person reporting that the plane was descending at 10,000 feet per minute.
The descent rate climbed to 20,000 feet per minute within seconds as an emergency was declared, and reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane began to bank.
About 35 seconds after the first mayday, the last words heard from the cockpit were "We're out of time".
Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said the plane's descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.
Videos on social media showed the jet slamming into the ground beside a road and bursting into flames.
"It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere," Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach.
"When you see that video, it's a jarring thing," he said.
Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said the impact left a "massive crater" near the entrance to a mobile home park.
About 600 residents were evacuated and moved to two shelters in the county, he said.
Forecaster AccuWeather said heavy rain and thunderstorms were hitting the area at the time.
The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash, which United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a "horrific tragedy".
Federal Aviation Administration records list the jet's owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based manufacturer Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: JS-SEZ sees RM40.3bil projects take off
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Some RM40.3 billion, or about 45 per cent, of the RM88.83 billion in approved investments under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) has been implemented, with projects across the zone expected to generate 28,755 jobs.
The implemented investments accounted for 12,796 potential employment opportunities, according to a joint statement issued following the inaugural Johor-Singapore Cooperation Ministerial Committee (JSCMC) meeting today.
The inaugural JSCMC meeting was held in Singapore and co-chaired by Malaysia's Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir and Singapore's National Development Minister Chee Hong Tat.
Between January 2025 and June 2026, the JS-SEZ recorded RM88.83 billion in approved investments under the purview of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority.
"The ministers welcomed the progress in investment realisation," it said.
Of the total approved investments, about 45 per cent had progressed to the implementation stage, reflecting the development momentum of the economic zone.
Both countries also welcomed investments from Singapore and Singapore-based companies referred to the Investment Facilitation Centre – Johor by Singapore.
"Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to ensuring that the institutional, regulatory and operational frameworks needed for the JS-SEZ are effectively put in place," it said.
Businesses exploring investment opportunities in the zone are being supported through Singapore's JS-SEZ Project Office and Malaysia's Invest Malaysia Facilitation Centre – Johor.
The JS-SEZ joint working committee also reported progress in infrastructure and utilities development, targeted investment missions and engagements, investment realisation, cross-border connectivity and talent development collaborations between the two countries.
The committee said infrastructure and utilities planning was being coordinated to align with the zone's overall development plans and anticipated investment requirements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore steps up vape crackdown, warns foreigners of re-entry bans
Article:
jashadiqe@nst.com.my
JOHOR BARU: Foreigners caught possessing, using or buying vapes in Singapore face tougher penalties, including possible bans on re-entering the republic.
The warning follows a four-day crackdown that uncovered 50 cases and resulted in the seizure of more than 5,476 vaping devices and related components.
The Singapore Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) said the cases were detected between Oct 26 and 29, with short-term visitors accounting for 68 per cent, while the remaining 32 per cent involved Singaporeans.
One of the biggest seizures was made at Changi Airport Terminal 4 on Oct 26, when officers flagged four arriving foreigners for further checks and found 5,272 vapes and related components in their luggage.
The four were referred to the Health Sciences Authority for further action under Singapore's Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act (TVCA).
Under the tougher enforcement measures, short-term visitors who reoffend may be barred from re-entering Singapore.
Long-term pass holders face possible revocation of their passes and deportation after a third offence, as well as a ban on returning to the republic.
Vaping is illegal in Singapore, and those caught possessing, using or purchasing vaporisers face penalties under the law.
The ICA said it had stepped up checks at the republic's air, land and sea checkpoints as part of a whole-of-government effort to curb the smuggling of vaporisers.
The intensified checks serve as a warning to travellers, including Malaysians who frequently cross the border, not to carry prohibited vaping devices into Singapore.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
