Title: Boustead taps MCorp to build leadership pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Boustead Holdings Bhd and PT MarkPlus Indonesia (MCorp) have partnered to strengthen the former's leadership pipeline and organisational capabilities as part of efforts to establish Boustead Academy.
The collaboration, led by Boustead's group human capital management division, is aimed at accelerating the company's transformation into a high-performance organisation through leadership development, a performance-driven culture and organisational improvements.
MCorp provides corporate education, market research, consulting, media and meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) services across Asia.
It also manages the Kotler Marketing Institute in collaboration with Kotler Marketing Group China.
Boustead chairman General Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Haji Zainal said the partnership supports the company's aspiration to make boustead great again by revitalising its organisational culture, unlocking employees' potential and creating sustainable long-term value.
"Ultimately, this strategic direction qualifies Boustead Group to fulfil the government's defence requirements, nurture local talent, strengthen domestic industrial capabilities and build a more resilient, self-reliant Malaysian defence industry ecosystem," he said at the memorandum of collaboration (MoC) signing ceremony today.
Abdul Aziz said the company's transformation involves more than a shift in business focus, requiring changes in leadership mindset, organisational culture and execution capabilities.
He said developing a high-performance organisation required continuous investment in employees, creating opportunities for professional growth and embedding the company's values in leadership and decision-making.
Boustead group managing director Ahmad Sabirin said the partnership reflected the company's commitment to developing talent, strengthening leadership and aligning its organisational culture with its evolving business ambitions.
"We want our people to have the clarity, confidence and competencies to perform their best while building careers within Boustead Group," he said.
The establishment of Boustead Academy is expected to support the company's ambition to strengthen its position in Malaysia's defence industry, in line with the objectives of the Defence Industry Policy of Malaysia.
The initiative will focus on developing local talent, advancing high-value manufacturing and technological innovation, exploring new business opportunities and strengthening public-private partnerships.
Boustead said its evolving business direction, particularly its ambition to expand its defence presence, requires leadership continuity, stronger organisational capabilities and a workforce equipped to meet changing business needs.
It also highlighted the need to prepare future leaders, preserve institutional knowledge and develop specialised expertise to support the company's long-term priorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pakatan files police report against BN’s Rim candidate over alleged use of govt assets in Melaka campaign, evidence to go to EC
Article:
JASIN, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has lodged a police report against Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate for the 16th Melaka state election, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, over allegations that she campaigned using government premises and machinery.
Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Central Leadership Council (MPP) member Siti Aishah Shaik Ismail said the police report against the incumbent for Rim state constituency was filed by a PH representative at the Jasin district police headquarters (IPD) today.
Aishah alleged that Khaidirah committed this act while attending an event where contributions were presented to approximately 30 recipients in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration with photographic evidence and recordings related to the incident have been submitted to the police.
“We have submitted evidence that (Khaidirah) misused the Rim Japerun Complex to host the event a venue that should no longer be used for politically-oriented programmes once the State Legislative Assembly has been dissolved, even though the building previously served as her office when she was the elected representative here.
“We also discovered that the food baskets she distributed bore the label ‘MPJ’ (Jasin Municipal Council), indicating that these were government-funded contributions,” she said during a press conference at the Pakatan Harapan (PH) main operations room for the Rim constituency in Jasin today.
Aishah said they also possess evidence showing several MPJ officials wearing attire that displayed the face of the Jasin Umno vice-chief throughout the contribution distribution event.
She added that all evidence regarding this matter would be submitted to the Election Commission (EC) tomorrow, and urged for an immediate, transparent, and independent investigation, as well as a proper explanation to be provided to the public.
“We do not dispute the people’s right to receive aid, especially with the upcoming Deepavali celebrations. Providing assistance to the public is a responsibility that must be fulfilled regardless of race, religion, or political affiliation.
“However, we view the involvement of a Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate in this programme very seriously, as it raises significant questions regarding the potential use of government machinery, premises, and facilities to grant an unfair advantage to a specific candidate during an ongoing election,” she said.
In this Melaka state election, PH has fielded Esma Eazreen Husin, the Jasin PKR Wanita wing Chief to contest the Rim seat in a one-on-one showdown against Khaidirah.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting scheduled for November 10. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: Police free two on bail, track more suspects with Indonesia’s help in tanker ketamine case
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — The police are currently tracking down several other individuals believed to be linked to the recent discovery of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine aboard a tanker.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said these individuals have been identified, and efforts to locate them are underway to assist with further investigations.
“We recently arrested two individuals, but their remand period has since expired. They have been released on police bail for the time being.
“Nevertheless, there are several other individuals we are tracking down to assist with the investigation,” he said when met at the NCID case evidence disposal event at Selangor police contingent headquarters (IPK) here today.
Hussein added that the police would continue to collaborate with Indonesian authorities to obtain further information regarding the case.
Media outlets previously reported that the police had detained two men, both aged 40, to assist in the investigation under Section 34 of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Commenting on the case of a Chinese national detained at Hong Kong International Airport on suspicion of transporting two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang, Hussein noted that the drug syndicate appears to have shifted away from using Malaysian citizens.
Instead, he explained that the police have identified several recurring modi operandi in which Chinese nationals are utilised as drug mules.
According to him, these individuals typically enter Malaysia via Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before traveling to Penang by land.
“They arrive at KLIA, travel to Penang, and then board a separate flight to Hong Kong while carrying the cocaine.”
“So far, there have been three cases; two individuals were successfully arrested in Hong Kong, while another was arrested by us in Penang,” he said.
Hussein said preliminary investigations indicate the operation is likely run by a syndicate, with a mastermind orchestrating the movements of the drug mules.
Authorities also believe the syndicate arranges for new passports for the Chinese nationals involved before they travel to Malaysia.
Commenting on the choice of Penang as a transit point, Hussein suggested that this tactic might be intended to mislead law enforcement by altering flight routes.
Media outlets previously reported that a 25-year-old Chinese national was detained at Hong Kong International Airport on October 22, suspected of carrying two kilogrammes (kg) of cocaine from Penang with the promised a payment of RMB 2,000 (approximately RM 1,200) to transport the drugs. — Bernama

Title: Investment, love and job scams: Nine locals among 141 arrested as Penang police bust 14 online call centres
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police arrested 141 individuals, including nine locals, in 14 raids on call centres suspected of conducting various online scam operations in the state from October 9 to 29.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the state Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) operation involved five raids in Timur Laut district, six in Barat Daya district, and three in Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT), following intelligence gathering and surveillance.
“In the raids, police arrested 93 Chinese nationals, 29 Vietnamese, four Japanese, three Taiwanese, two Cambodians, one Myanmar national, and nine locals, all aged between 18 and 48.
“They are from different groups or syndicates believed to be involved in investment scams, love scams, impersonation of police officers, and non-existent job offers using various platforms such as WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok,” he told a press conference at the Penang Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
He said the syndicates are believed to have rented houses in recent months to carry out their operations, using Penang as a base to target victims mainly overseas, including in China, Japan, the United States, Brazil and Hong Kong.
Lim said police also seized equipment, including mobile phones, laptops, tablets, internet routers, electronic equipment and computer accessories, believed to be used in the syndicates’ operations, valued at RM1.4 million.
He added police were investigating potential abuse of immigration passes and facilities for illegal activities, although most foreigners detained entered Malaysia legally with valid passports.
All suspects have been remanded, and the case is being investigated under Section 420 read together with Section 120B of the Penal Code, as well as Section 6(3) and Section 15(1)© of the Immigration Act 1959/63. — Bernama

Title: Police rule out racial, gang links in Desa Tun Razak clash; seek 15 more suspects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have ruled out racial and gang-related elements in an altercation involving a group of individuals outside a cafe in Desa Tun Razak, Sungai Besi, last night.
Cheras police chief ACP Mohd Rosdi Daud said preliminary investigations suggested that the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a business turf dispute, although investigations were ongoing to establish the actual cause.
“We urge the public not to speculate about the incident as investigations are still ongoing,” he told a press conference at the Cheras district police headquarters here today.
He said police had arrested nine people, including a woman, aged between 16 and 44, to assist in the investigation and seized several items believed to have been used in the incident.
Two of those arrested, aged 32 and 44, were identified as the main suspects.
“All nine were remanded for one to three days, while six had previous criminal and drug-related records,” he said.
Police are also tracking down about 15 others believed to have been involved in the incident.
The case is being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting with weapons.
Earlier, Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed that nine people had been arrested by a team from the Sungai Besi Police Station’s Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit and the Cheras district police headquarters’ Criminal Investigation Division.
The arrests were made near the scene after police received information about a fight involving a group of people at about 11pm. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest man at Penang airport over RM3.2m cannabis bound for London; RM1.05m drugs seized in Jelutong
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Police arrested a local man in possession of 40 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds, valued at RM3.2 million, which were allegedly being smuggled to London. The arrest took place during a raid at Penang International Airport (PIA) in Bayan Lepas on October 18.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the 28-year-old man, who hails from Miri, Sarawak, was apprehended at about 5pm while in the airport’s waiting area and the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage.
“Preliminary investigations revealed that the man, acting as a ‘drug mule,’ claimed he was instructed by an individual to transport the drugs to London. It is believed that this was the suspect’s first time participating in cross-border drug smuggling via air travel.
“The suspect allegedly acted as a courier, receiving a payment of RM9,000 for the trip,” he said during a press conference at the Penang contingent police headquarters here today.
He added that an initial urine screening test indicated that the man who is currently unemployed tested positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine. A background check further revealed that he has two prior criminal records.
In a separate case, Lim said police arrested three individuals, including a Chinese national woman, during a raid at an apartment in Jelutong here yesterday evening. Various types of drugs with an estimated value of RM1.05 million were seized.
He explained that police first apprehended a 26-year-old local man in front of the apartment’s elevator, discovering a 1.3-gramme (g) packet of ketamine in his possession. Subsequently, they arrested a 40-year-old Chinese national woman on the 10th floor of the apartment, who is believed to be involved in the processing and distribution of drugs.
“A search of one of the rooms in the apartment uncovered seven kilogrammes (kg) of methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA) powder, Erimin-5 pills (35g), ketamine (20g), and 0.015 litre of liquid methamphetamine (‘syabu’). Additionally, authorities seized equipment for repackaging the MDMA, including a digital scale and packaging materials,” he said.
Lim noted that the woman is believed to have been responsible for repackaging the MDMA, which was then sold to customers who would arrive at the apartment to collect the drugs, following the procurement of supplies from a distribution network drugs.
He said another local man, aged 44 believed to have arrived to purchase drugs was also arrested in front of the apartment.
He added that urine screening tests revealed two of the suspects tested positive for ketamine, while another tested positive for cannabis; a check of their past records showed that all three had prior records related to criminal and narcotics offences.
They have all been remanded to assist with the investigation under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Operasi Payung: Education Ministry boosts flood prep for SPM candidates, says deputy D-G
Article:
KUALA NERUS, Nov 2 — The Education Ministry is stepping up preparations for the North-east Monsoon (MTL) to ensure that Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates in flood-prone areas can sit for their examinations safely and comfortably through Operasi Payung.
Education (School Operations Sector) deputy director-general Datuk Zainal Abas said the annual operation was aimed at helping candidates in flood-affected areas sit for their examinations without disruption.
He said candidates in areas at risk of flooding would be given special arrangements during the written examinations.
“For example, SPM candidates living on islands in Terengganu will be brought to the mainland and accommodated at fully residential schools. This will prevent them from having to cross rough seas during the monsoon season to reach their examination centres.
“It will also provide a safer and more suitable working environment for teachers serving as examination personnel,” he told reporters after the Terafecta Digital Luminaries Awards ceremony organised by the Terengganu State Education Department (JPNT) at Dewan Jubli Perak, Bandar Baru Kuala Nerus here today.
Zainal said the ministry was also coordinating preparations with the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), state and district disaster management committees and other relevant agencies to assist areas at risk of flooding.
On schools designated as temporary relief centres (PPS), he said Nadma had allocated more than RM7 million this year to help the ministry improve their facilities.
The allocation covered toilet repairs and school maintenance to ensure the facilities were in good condition to accommodate flood victims.
“Recently, we were also informed that Nadma would provide an additional RM5 million to support the ministry’s post-North-east Monsoon efforts,” he said.
He advised schools, parents and students to remain vigilant and take the necessary safety precautions throughout the monsoon season.
Parents, particularly those living in flood-prone areas, were urged to keep a close watch on their children to prevent accidents.
“Children playing in floodwaters or near drains during floods can put themselves in danger. Parents should therefore pay closer attention to their children’s safety. Health and hygiene must also be prioritised,” he said.
Zainal said the ministry was also ready to deploy its Smart Support Team (SST), comprising counselling teachers, to provide mental health support programmes and activities for primary school pupils.
The Academic Support Team (AST) would also assist students affected by floods, including by providing academic support at temporary relief centres.
“Although the school holidays begin on December 5, these teams can still be deployed to flood relief centres if schools are affected by floods in November, particularly to support examination candidates,” he said.
He expressed hope that preparations and coordination with Nadma, state disaster management committees, the police (PDRM), the Civil Defence Force (APM) and other agencies would proceed smoothly to address any eventuality during the monsoon season.
The 2026 SPM written examinations will be held from November 23 to December 17, while the North-east Monsoon began on October 27 and is expected to continue until March 2027. — Bernama

Title: KL to get 22km of covered walkways under RM55m project starting Jan 2027, says Hannah Yeoh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Putrajaya will spend RM55 million to build the covered pedestrian walkways across the capital city, with the start of work scheduled for January 2027, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Parliament this evening.
Under Kuala Lumpur City Hall’s (DBKL) operating expenditure, 22 kilometres of covered walkways will be built across Kuala Lumpur’s parliamentary constituencies, with an allocation of two kilometres per constituency, she said.
Yeoh said the project is expected to be completed by the third quarter of next year.
“While no pedestrian walkways are currently under construction, implementation for next year will begin as early as January 2027,” the minister said when winding up the third stage reading of Budget 2027.
The new rollout follows the success of previous projects from 2023 to date, which span 29 locations totalling 4.35 kilometres.
Yeoh said the walkways are designed to bridge critical urban gaps by connecting residential zones, public facilities, commercial hubs, bus stops, health clinics and places of worship.
DBKL will also construct an additional 20 kilometres of covered pedestrian walkways in the city centre to connect public transport facilities to destinations such as commercial centres, office complexes, and park facilities like the Botanical Garden and Titiwangsa Lake Garden, she added.
The project was first announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when he tabled Budget 2027.
Under this federal budget, DBKL received a dedicated allocation to roll out urban infrastructure enhancements as part of a broader RM400 million package aimed at green spaces, parks, and public facility upgrades.
City-centre traffic congestion has worsened over the years, which public transport analysts blame on car-centric policies and subsidies that keep petrol price artificially cheap.
Yeoh had said that the infrastructure is meant to encourage citizens to walk or use public transit instead of driving.

Title: Demand for ETS, EMUPlus tickets for Deepavali exceeds offered capacity as 100,304 tickets sold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) has recorded the sale of 100,304 tickets for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and EMUPlus services for the Deepavali period, covering travel dates from November 5 to November 10.
KTMB group chief executive officer Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the high demand reflects a positive public response to the rail services during the festive season.
He noted that the seating capacity offered has increased by 70 per cent compared to the same festive period last year.
He made these remarks following an event with Deputy Minister of National Unity, R. Yuneswaran to distribute 600 Deepavali gift packs to ETS passengers at KL Sentral here today.
KTMB had previously announced an additional 14,384 seats across its ETS and EMUPlus services to meet passenger demand for the festival.
Separately, KTMB has also opened ticket sales for its ETS and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) services for travel between January and February 2027, effective from 12 noon today.
A total of 1.57 million seats are being offered via ETS and ERT services for the first quarter of next year.
According to a press statement, 102,819 tickets have already been sold as of today from the additional capacity made available for that period.
KTMB advises the public to plan their journeys in advance, purchase tickets through official channels, and arrive at the station at least 30 minutes before the scheduled departure time to ensure a smoother and more comfortable travel experience throughout the festive season. — Bernama

Title: Border control agency DG Shuhaily returns to duty after leave
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 2 — The director-general of the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, resumed his duties at the agency today, following reports that he had been on leave last week.
In a post on its official Facebook page, AKPS said Mohd Shuhaily began his duties by chairing the ‘Commander’s Call’ Meeting No. 3/2026.
“The meeting, which brought together all entry point senior officers and commanders of AKPS, focused on ‘2027 Deployment Plan’ (Gerak Atur 2027).
“It specifically addressed strengthening the strategic direction, operational readiness, and the effectiveness of the nation’s border control and protection with a clear focus and streamlined operations as the mission continues,” said AKPS.
The agency remains committed to strengthening operational efficiency, integrity, and security at the nation’s entry points.
In the post, AKPS also included six photographs showing Mohd Shuhaily chairing a meeting attended by the agency’s top leadership.
Those present included AKPS deputy director-general (operations), Datuk Mohd Nasaruddin M Nasir; AKPS deputy director-general (policy), Zuraini Othman; and AKPS Commander for Port Klang, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
Previously, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) had decided that Mohd Shuhaily would return to service with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Mohd Shuhaily was appointed as the director-general of AKPS for a two-year term, from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2027.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to two charges of causing injury to two police officers at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on Sept 28. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin calls for stern action over alleged halal breaches at Puchong chicken plant
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has called for stern action, including prosecution, against the operator or owner of a chicken processing plant that recently sparked concern among the Muslim community.
He said local authorities and halal certification bodies must strengthen cooperation in monitoring such premises, conducting investigations and gathering information from the public.
“Halal certification bodies and local authorities must conduct regular inspections to ensure that sensitive operations, particularly those involving health and hygiene, are closely monitored.
“I also urge the relevant parties to consider stern action, including prosecution, based on the findings of thorough investigations,” he said when met at Sekolah Rendah Agama Integrasi (SRAI) in Section 19 here today.
Also present were Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzil Ahmad and Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) director Datuk Shahzihan Ahmad, who joined Amirudin in distributing 1,321 food packs under the Nutrisi Selangor (NutriSel) programme.
JAIS seized more than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken worth RM85,400 during Ops Taring Chiller at a warehouse in Puchong last Saturday (October 31) after finding that the slaughtering process did not comply with Islamic requirements.
Meanwhile, Amirudin also issued a stern warning following the discovery of illicit substances allegedly concealed at an unauthorised place of worship in South Klang during raids conducted by the Selangor Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) from October 13 to 19.
“Immoral or criminal activities must not be concealed behind places of worship. I leave it to the authorities to take firm action, as such conduct is detrimental to society and damages the reputation of religious institutions.
“We cannot hold everyone responsible, but if an incident occurs at a particular location, appropriate action must be taken. No protection will be given to those involved in unlawful activities,” he said.
On October 23, Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said a local man had been arrested to assist in investigations into alleged drug trafficking activities involving an unregistered place of worship in Klang that was used to store drugs. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia: Thunderstorms and heavy rain to lash all 13 states, three Federal Territories until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds are forecast across all 13 states and three Federal Territories until 7pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
In an advisory issued today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather is expected across all of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Selangor, and Melaka, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
In Perak, the affected areas include Kampar, Kinta, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Selama, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Kerian, Larut, Matang, and Manjung.
Similar conditions are forecast in the East Coast states of Kelantan (Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, and Jeli), Terengganu (Kemaman, Dungun, and Hulu Terengganu), and Pahang (Kuantan, Pekan, Jerantut, Maran, Rompin, and Cameron Highlands).
In Negeri Sembilan, the warning covers Tampin, Rembau, Port Dickson, and Seremban, while in Johor, the affected districts are Pontian, Johor Bahru, Kulai, Tangkak, Muar, Batu Pahat, and Segamat.
In Sarawak, the areas involved are Kuching, Samarahan, Betong, Mukah, Bintulu, Sibu, Serian, Limbang, Sarikei, Sri Aman (Pantu, Lingga, and Sri Aman), and Miri (Subis).
The department also forecast similar weather for the Federal Territory of Labuan and parts of Sabah, covering Tawau, the West Coast, Kudat (Kota Marudu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Labuk, Sugut, Telupid, Sandakan, and Paitan), and the Interior division (Pensiangan, Membakut, Tambunan, Beaufort, Sipitang, and Kuala Penyu). — Bernama

Title: Four days of hybrid lectures from Nov 9 to 13 for IPG trainees during Deepavali, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The Education Ministry (MOE) will provide four days of hybrid lectures for trainee teachers at Institute of Teacher Education (IPG) campuses in conjunction with Deepavali.
Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the facility would be available from November 9 to 12 for Group A, comprising Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, and from November 10 to 13 for Group B, covering Perlis, Penang, Perak, Selangor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Pahang, Sabah and the Federal Territories.
“Through this arrangement, trainee teachers returning home to celebrate Deepavali can continue attending lectures online. IPG campuses may also apply for additional leave and replacement holidays if necessary,” she said in a Facebook post today.
She said the measure would ensure that trainee teachers could continue their studies while spending time with their families during the festival.
Fadhlina also extended her Deepavali greetings to all trainee teachers and their families celebrating the festival.
Deepavali, also known as the Festival of Lights, falls on November 8 this year and is an important Hindu festival symbolising the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil. — Bernama

Title: Police record Penang assemblyman’s statement over alleged assault on wife
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — Penang police have confirmed receiving a report from the wife of an assemblyman who alleged that she was assaulted by her husband at their residence here last Saturday.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said police were conducting further investigations into the incident, with an investigation paper opened under Section 323 of the Penal Code.
“Police have recorded statements from four individuals, including the husband and wife, and no arrests have been made so far in connection with the case.
“The investigation paper will be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further instructions,” he told reporters at a press conference at the Penang Police Contingent Headquarters here today.
Lim also denied claims by the assemblyman’s wife that police had failed to take action on the report she lodged.
He stressed that the police had taken the appropriate action upon receiving the report and would also obtain medical confirmation regarding the injuries allegedly sustained by the woman. — Bernama

Title: Mall manager, father file police reports over woman’s alleged harassment at KL shopping mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police have received two reports concerning three incidents involving a woman accused of harassing visitors at a shopping mall here.
Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the first report was lodged by the building manager at 7.59 pm yesterday following complaints that the woman had caused public disturbance.
The second report was lodged by the father of two children, who alleged that the woman had pushed and assaulted his children in an incident on the same day.
“The case is being investigated under Sections 323 and 506 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation,” he said in a statement today.
Ahmad Azwan said police viewed seriously any acts of violence, threats or harassment against members of the public, particularly those involving children’s safety.
He added that appropriate action would be taken against anyone found to have committed an offence.
Yesterday, police confirmed that they had detected a 35-second video circulating on social media showing an argument between two individuals at the shopping mall.
The incident reportedly occurred at about 3 pm when a 36-year-old man and his two children, aged two and seven, were approached by an unidentified woman.
The woman allegedly pushed the man’s son from behind, causing him to fall, and struck his daughter on the back of her head.
Ahmad Azwan urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2146 0522 or 03-2146 0585, the Dang Wangi District Police Control Centre at 03-2600 2222, or any nearby police station to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: No licence: Cops probe driver as three family members killed, teenage girl seriously injured in Tawau crash
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 2 — Three members of a family were killed while a 15-year-old girl was seriously injured after the car they were travelling in skidded off the road at Batu 14, Jalan Apas, here at about 9.30am today.
Tawau police chief ACP Rosdi Mat Jusoh said the deceased were a 50-year-old woman and her two sons, aged 30 and 28, who were pronounced dead at the scene at 10.16am.
He said the family was travelling from Kampung Bahagia, Sandakan, to Tawau when the 28-year-old son, who was driving, allegedly lost control of the car along a straight stretch of road.
The vehicle skidded onto the left shoulder, crashed into an oil palm tree, travelled about 60 metres before overturning and coming to a stop.
The teenage girl, who was seated in the back with her mother, sustained injuries to her abdomen and ribs.
In a statement today, Rosdi said initial checks found that the driver did not have a driving licence. The vehicle had been seized for inspection by the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (PUSPAKOM).
Police are also seeking independent witnesses to help determine the cause of the accident.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Rosdi reminded motorists to exercise caution and comply with traffic regulations. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Govt boosts MAF senior officers’ career paths in recognition of their role
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The government has agreed to improve the career progression of senior Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) officers in recognition of their heavy responsibilities in defending national sovereignty and security, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the agreement was reached during a special meeting with MAF’s top leadership, which he chaired today.
He noted that the move aligns with the need to strengthen national defence capabilities amid an increasingly complex and challenging global security and geostrategic landscape.
“The meeting also provided an opportunity for us to examine the readiness of each service branch, as well as the procurement and maintenance needs of defence assets, to ensure the MAF’s operational capabilities remain at their peak,” he said in a Facebook post.
Anwar said he valued direct input and feedback from the MAF leadership, emphasising that every government policy and decision must be based on actual needs on the ground rather than mere considerations on paper.
The Prime Minister assured that the Madani government will continue to pay close attention to the welfare and needs of MAF personnel.
“Defending the sovereignty and peace of our homeland is not solely the responsibility of the security forces, but a sacred trust that we must uphold together,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No unhealthy API readings as monsoon winds to cut transboundary haze, improve air quality, says DOE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Air quality is expected to improve further amid increasingly humid conditions and more frequent rainfall in several areas, as well as a downgrade in regional haze alert levels by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC).
Department of Environment (DOE) Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said that although fire hotspots were still being detected in several parts of Southeast Asia, changing wind patterns associated with the monsoon transition and the onset of the Northeast Monsoon (NEM) were expected to help reduce transboundary haze entering Malaysia.
She said winds that typically blow from the northeast towards the southwest could potentially reduce the influx of smoke from Sumatra into Peninsular Malaysia.
Azuri Azizah said the DOE’s latest monitoring showed that air quality in most parts of Malaysia was improving.
“As of today, no monitoring stations have recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at the unhealthy level or higher. However, the DOE will continue to monitor the country’s air quality closely,” she told Bernama.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, 39 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings as of 3pm today, while 29 areas recorded good air quality.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah advised the public to remain alert to API readings in their respective areas and follow advice issued by the authorities. — Bernama

Title: Teoh Beng Hock family knew for seven years death wasn’t probed as murder, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The High Court here was told today that the family of Teoh Beng Hock has been aware for more than seven years that the death of the then political secretary in 2009 had never been investigated as a murder case.
Senior Federal Counsel Mohammad Sallehuddin Md Ali raised the matter in the government’s preliminary objection to the fresh judicial review application filed by Beng Hock’s family on April 17 this year.
According to Mohammad Sallehuddin, the investigation into Beng Hock’s death in 2009 had actually been reclassified under Section 342 of the Penal Code for wrongful confinement in 2019.
He noted that while the family had previously complained about the slow pace of the investigation and questioned whether the matter had been referred to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC), they had delayed taking legal action.
“Despite their knowledge, they only filed the application to commence a judicial review now, which has exceeded the statutory deadline of three months.
“Pursuant to Order 53 Rule 3(6) of the Rules of Court 2012, the three-month period for the family to seek leave for judicial review began on June 28, 2019, the date of a letter from the applicants’ previous lawyer questioning the classification of the investigation under Section 342 of the Penal Code, and expired on September 29, 2019,” he said.
In response, lawyer Lim Wei Jiet, representing Beng Hock’s family, countered that they had written to the police and the Attorney General in the past.
However, they never received any confirmation on whether the investigations was being conducted under Section 302 for murder or Section 304 for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
“But now they come to court today claiming we are out of time. If the court agrees with them, we urge the court to grant an extension of time. This case has generated massive public interest for many years, yet the family has been left completely in the dark about what happened to him,” Lim said. Beng Hock’s parents were present in court today.
Judge Norliza Othman then fixed November 17 to deliver the ruling on whether to grant the family’s request for an extension of time.
On April 17 this year, the deceased’s brother, Teoh Meng Kee, and parents, Teoh Leong Hwee and Teng Shuw Hoi, filed an application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings. They named the Inspector-General of Police, PDRM Criminal Investigation Department director, PDRM, Attorney-General and the Government of Malaysia as the first to fifth respondents.
The applicants are seeking a declaration that the respondents have a legal duty to initiate an investigation into Beng Hock’s death on July 16, 2009, under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, or culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 of the Penal Code and seeking the mandamus order to compel the respondents to complete the investigation within 120 days from the date of the court order.
On November 21, 2024, the High Court here ordered PDRM to complete the investigation into Beng Hock’s death within six months after allowing a judicial review application by the deceased’s parents.
However, on May 20, 2025, the Criminal Investigation Department of the Selangor Police Contingent Headquarters wrote a letter to the family’s former lawyer stating that the investigation had been conducted under the offence of wrongful confinement pursuant to Section 342 of the Penal Code, and that the Attorney General’s Chambers had decided to take No Further Action (NFA) on the matter.
Beng Hock, who was then political secretary to Seri Kembangan assemblyman Ean Yong Hian Wah, was found dead at the Plaza Masalam building in Shah Alam after having given a statement at the MACC office on the 14th floor.
On January 5, 2011, the Shah Alam Coroner’s Court returned an open verdict, ruling that Beng Hock’s death in 2009 was neither a suicide nor a homicide, and finding that no third party was involved in his death.
Subsequently, on July 21, 2011, the Royal Commission of Inquiry established to investigate Beng Hock’s death ruled that his death was by suicide. On September 5, 2014, the Court of Appeal reversed the open verdict in Beng Hock’s death case and ruled that his death resulted from an unlawful act committed by one or more unidentified persons. — Bernama

Title: Klang Valley flash floods hit Denai Alam, TTDI, Bukit Jalil, Subang and more
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Heavy rain triggered flash floods across several parts of the Klang Valley this afternoon, leaving roads inundated, disrupting traffic and flooding residential and commercial areas.
Videos and photographs shared on social media showed flooding in Denai Alam, Taman Tun Dr Ismail (TTDI), Bukit Jalil, Subang and along the Federal Highway near Amcorp Mall in Petaling Jaya.
In Denai Alam, Threads user @iskandarsukandar shared footage of heavy rain reducing visibility, with several motorists apparently turning back.
“What happened in Denai Alam? Everyone is turning back against the flow of traffic. Is Denai Alam flooded?” the user wrote, later identifying Persiaran Ficus as an affected road.
Another user, @eg1e___, reported severe flooding near a water tank area and a fallen tree near a Petronas station, while @kiti.ss shared footage of flooding along a route through Elmina.
Berita Harian
also reported that motorists entering Denai Alam from the Damansara-Shah Alam Elevated Expressway (DASH) were forced to turn back, with flooding reported along the road from Johawaki towards Caltex Denai Alam.
In Kampung Melayu Subang, Threads user @hasfiyayasmin reported severe flooding, claiming water levels had risen above chest height.
Photographs accompanying the post showed a flooded residential street and water rising to the windows of a house.
Meanwhile, user @zarrinloqman shared photographs showing a parking area near Proton in Subang inundated, with several parked vehicles partially submerged.
Astro Radio Traffic
reported at 3.27pm that flash floods along the Federal Highway near Amcorp Mall had caused heavy traffic between Templer and KL Gateway.
It also reported slow-moving traffic along Jalan Bukit Pantai in Bangsar due to flooding, sharing videos credited to Threads user @slmanfrish.
According to
Berita Harian
, vehicles were also seen navigating flooded roads in TTDI, while rising water levels were reported along the route from Bukit Jalil towards Puchong.
Heavy rain and strong winds were also reported near Rosyam Mart in USJ 9, Subang Jaya.

Title: Cheras police custodial death: Three lawyers questioned over alleged harassment of doctor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police are investigating allegations that several lawyers harassed a forensic specialist in connection with the death of detainee Noorizwan Zulkefly.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said police had received a report from the doctor and were investigating the case under Sections 506, 186 and 189 of the Penal Code.
“The doctor is a civil servant and a police report has been lodged by her. Investigations are ongoing, and police are recording statements from the parties concerned,” he told a press conference at Bukit Aman here today.
He said police had so far recorded statements from the doctor and three lawyers linked to the case, while statements from Noorizwan’s family members were being taken.
On the investigation into Noorizwan’s death, Kumar said the investigation papers would be referred to the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) on Wednesday for further action.
He had earlier said that the investigation into Noorizwan’s death had been taken over by the Prosecution/Legal Division (D5) of Bukit Aman CID and was being conducted under Section 331 of the Penal Code.
The classification followed a statement recorded from a forensic medicine consultant at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, which indicated external injuries on several parts of the deceased’s body.
The pattern of injuries was consistent with blunt-force trauma and not self-inflicted.
However, the full post-mortem report confirming the cause of death has yet to be received, and the police are awaiting further information. — Bernama

Title: Fire partially destroys KTMB cargo train in Johor Bahru, no casualties reported
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 2 — A Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cargo train was partially damaged by a fire while travelling at Kilometre 4.75 near Taman Daya here today.
No casualties were reported in the incident.
Tebrau Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Nor Azmi Maryono said the train was travelling from Kempas Baru station to Pasir Gudang station when the incident occurred.
He said the Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 1.26pm.
Firefighters work to extinguish a fire involving a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cargo train locomotive near Taman Daya in Johor Bahru on November 2, 2026. — Picture courtesy of the Johor Fire and Rescue Department
“Following this, seven personnel, supported by a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) vehicle, were immediately dispatched to the scene, about six kilometres away.
“Upon arrival, the responding team found that the fire involved the cargo train’s locomotive, with damage estimated at five per cent,” he said in a statement today.
Nor Azmi said firefighting operations were still ongoing, and the cause of the fire had yet to be determined.
Pictures of the incident had earlier circulated on social media.

Title: No need to stockpile food, Malaysia has at least six months of supply, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Malaysia has sufficient food supply capacity for at least six months and sees no need for emergency stockpiling measures despite concerns over potential disruptions to essential supplies, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the government continued to ensure national food security and adequate supplies of essential goods for Malaysians and others residing in the country.
“We see no need for such measures because our food security and stock levels are sufficient.
“We know that we have the capacity to sustain food security for at least six months,” he told reporters after attending the Malaysia-China Cooperation Meeting on Investment, Trade and Economic Empowerment here today.
Ahmad Zahid was responding to reports that several countries had advised their citizens to stockpile food and essential supplies in preparation for possible emergencies.
The Deputy Prime Minister stressed that Malaysia was not facing an emergency that would require the public to stock up on basic necessities.
“We are not in a state of emergency and, Insya-Allah, we are far from such a situation,” he said.
Previously, at least 33 countries were reportedly issuing preparedness guidelines encouraging citizens to keep emergency supplies of food, drinking water and other essentials.
According to international media reports, the advisories were prompted by various global threats, including armed conflicts, extreme weather, power outages and cyberattacks.
Among the countries stepping up preparedness campaigns are France and the United Kingdom, which have advised households to maintain at least 72 hours, or three days, of essential supplies. — Bernama

Title: AirAsia advises guests to plan ahead as year-end travel peak meets monsoon season
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 2 — AirAsia has advised guests travelling during the year-end peak travel period to plan ahead and allow sufficient time for their journeys amid increased passenger traffic and potentially adverse weather conditions.
The airline said the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which began on October 27 and is expected to continue until March next year, could bring prolonged periods of heavy rain, particularly between November and January, potentially causing flooding and disruptions to flight operations due to thunderstorms and adverse weather.
“Guests are encouraged to stay informed and take the necessary precautions before travelling,” it said in a statement today, while recommending all guests take note of the following advisory.
Among others, guests are advised to check their flight status regularly through its official website, particularly 24 hours before departure and again before leaving for the airport, and to arrive at the airport at least three hours before departure for international flights and two hours for domestic flights.
“All guests, including those travelling under group bookings, are strongly encouraged to complete self check-in via the AirAsia MOVE app or our airasia.com. Self check-in is available from 14 days up to one hour before the scheduled departure time,” the statement read.
The airline also advised guests to allow additional time for airport transfers as heavy rain, flooding and traffic congestion could affect road conditions and journey times.
For convenient access to KLIA Terminal 2, guests are encouraged to use the Express Rail Link (ERL).
According to the statement, guests can use airport kiosks to print baggage tags and complete self-bag drop, while counter check-in services will be limited to guests with reduced mobility, those travelling with infants below 24 months, pregnant women, senior citizens and young guests travelling alone.
At the same time, AirAsia reminded guests to ensure their email addresses and mobile numbers in their bookings are updated to receive important flight notifications and updates.
“Those travelling to or from destinations affected by severe weather should check local forecasts and follow instructions issued by the relevant authorities,” it said.
Malaysian passport holders travelling internationally are also encouraged to download the MyNIISe or MyBorderPass app in advance to facilitate immigration clearance at KLIA Terminal 2.
In the event of flight disruptions, AirAsia said guests are advised to check their emails for updates and available self-service options, where applicable, or seek further assistance through AirAsia’s chatbot, Bo.
“Guests requiring mobility assistance can pre-book wheelchair services when making their reservations or through the ‘My Bookings’ section on the AirAsia MOVE app at least four hours before departure,” the statement read.
The airline also reminded guests that cabin baggage is limited to one piece measuring no more than 56 x 36 x 23 centimetres and one laptop bag, handbag or small bag, with the combined weight of both items not exceeding seven kilogrammes.
As for pregnant guests, they are required to complete a form at the counter before boarding, while those more than 27 weeks pregnant must submit an approved medical certificate from a doctor.
AirAsia said it would continue monitoring operational conditions and provide relevant updates to affected guests through the contact details provided in their bookings. — Bernama

Title: Two friends plead not guilty to attempted RM8.2m jewellery robbery in Brickfields
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Two friends pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to attempting to rob a jewellery supplier of valuables worth RM8.2 million last month.
Salesman Tan Kah Seng, 35, and mechanic Tan Chien Ann, 30, were jointly charged with attempting to rob Toung Zheng Fay, 30, of three bags containing various types of jewellery while armed with a machete in front of a hotel in Brickfields at 10am on October 14.
The charge was framed under Sections 393 and 397 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code. Section 393 carries a maximum jail term of seven years and a fine, while Section 397 provides for imprisonment of up to 14 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Syafika Azwa Fikri did not offer bail, citing the non-bailable nature of the offence and the high value of the jewellery involved.
Lawyer Revin Kumar requested bail for both his clients, saying that Kah Seng was married and supporting his eight-year-old child, wife and parents, who suffer from health issues.
“Chien Ann, meanwhile, is divorced and earns RM2,000 a month. He supports his nine-year-old son and parents,” Revin said.
Judge Noor Aini Yusof set bail at RM15,000 with one surety for each of the accused and fixed November 30 for mention. — Bernama

Title: Long-term solution needed for Langkawi ferry lane sedimentation, says Loke
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 2 — The issue of sedimentation along the ferry lane in the waters of Kuala Kedah requires a more sustainable, long-term solution to ensure the smooth operation of ferry services to Langkawi.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said dredging works are carried out periodically every two years to prevent sedimentation from disrupting operations in the area.
However, he noted that a more comprehensive solution must be sought, given that this issue continues to be an operational constraint at the terminal.
“There are physical constraints because the passenger terminal currently under development is situated at its original location. Reclaiming land from the sea or developing new areas would be prohibitively expensive.
“Therefore, we are seeking a long-term solution to address this sedimentation issue, while dredging works are being carried out periodically,” he said.
He told reporters after officiating a ceremony to distribute special financial aid to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers in the state of Kedah here today.
Meanwhile, Loke encouraged both existing and new ferry operators to expand their services and increase trip frequencies to better meet the needs of users.
However, he noted that any increase in the number of trips would depend on the operators’ capabilities, taking into account various factors such as operating costs, passenger volume, and operational constraints.
Regarding the development of the new Kuala Kedah passenger terminal slated for completion in September 2027 he said the facility is expected to enhance the operational capacity of ferry services at the terminal.
He explained that the new facility will allow up to three ferries to dock simultaneously, compared to the current capacity of only one ferry at a time.
At the event, 351 taxi and rental car drivers from Kedah and Perlis received aid vouchers worth RM1,000 each.
Also present were Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Ministry of Transport secretary-general Datuk Seri Jana Santhiran Muniayan, and director-general of the Land Public Transport Agency Ahmad Radhi Maarof. — Bernama

Title: Document public sector expertise, institutional knowledge before it is lost, says public service chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Government agencies must systematically document their administrative experience and expertise to prevent the loss of institutional knowledge when civil servants retire or are transferred.
Public Service Director-General (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said knowledge gained through administrative work and research should be preserved and translated into policies, decisions and practical measures.
“Documented experience becomes institutional knowledge that builds the collective memory of the public service,” he said in his keynote address at the opening of the 2026 Research Colloquium at the National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN) here today.
His speech was read by INTAN director Datuk Dr Mohd Zabri Yusoff.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan urged government agencies to document project implementation experiences and administrative challenges through case studies and action research findings.
He also called on department heads and senior management to incorporate research findings into decision-making.
“Every study presented at this colloquium should be assessed for actions that can be taken by the respective organisations. Do not let these studies become mere documents gathering dust on library shelves,” he said.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan also expressed hope that the proposed restructuring of INTAN, particularly efforts to strengthen its Research and Consultancy Centre, would enhance its capacity to conduct applied research addressing current challenges faced by government agencies.
The event also saw the launch of a book titled *Penyelidikan Sektor Awam Malaysia: Pendekatan Kajian Tindakan* (Malaysian Public Sector Research: An Action Research Approach), intended as a reference for civil servants and researchers seeking to promote impact-driven research.
The two-day colloquium, organised by the Public Service Department through INTAN in strategic collaboration with Universiti Utara Malaysia, brings together 800 participants and features 41 research papers across four key clusters: technology and digitalisation, economics, social issues and sustainability, and public policy. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan challenges MCA to debates in all four seats they contest
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 2 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has proposed holding open debates with Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates from MCA contesting four seats in the 16th Melaka state election, expanding a challenge initially directed at its candidate for the Banda Hilir seat.
PH Melaka deputy chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the proposal followed MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong’s challenge to the PH candidate for Banda Hilir to hold a debate in the constituency.
“PH therefore proposes that the debate be expanded to involve candidates from both parties in all four constituencies contested by MCA and PH.
“Our four candidates are Low Chee Leong for Kota Laksamana, Leng Chau Yen for Banda Hilir, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir for Kelebang and Ginie Lim for Machap Jaya,” he told a daily PH press conference at Bukit Piatu here today.
Also present was DAP National Political Education Director Howard Lee Chuan How.
Khoo, who is also Melaka DAP chairman, said the debates could be held at a neutral venue agreed upon by both sides, with an independent non-governmental organisation (NGO) acting as mediator to ensure fair discussions.
He also proposed that the debates be conducted in Bahasa Melayu so that Melaka residents from diverse backgrounds could understand the arguments and positions presented by both sides.
“The debates could be held as soon as possible, before November 14,” he said.
Meanwhile, Lee said PH had also proposed debates involving the top leadership of both parties to discuss national policies affecting Melaka.
He said open debates would provide a platform for both sides to explain their respective policies and positions to the people, while encouraging transparent competition of ideas as part of democratic practice.
Polling is on November 14, with early voting set for November 10.
For updates on the state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/
. — Bernama

Title: Lim Guan Eng urges Penang govt to freeze tax hikes, scrutinise major projects
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — DAP’s Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng has urged the Penang government to defer increases in land tax, water tariffs and other fees until the end of its term, saying the state’s improved financial position should allow it to avoid placing further pressure on residents and businesses.
Debating the 2027 Supply Bill and Development Estimates in the Penang State Legislative Assembly today, Lim said he supported the RM1.074 billion state budget, noting that the Consolidated Revenue Account balance had increased from RM522.87 million at the end of 2025 to RM651.28 million as at October 30 this year, while Penang’s gross domestic product grew 7.3 per cent to RM130.3 billion in 2025, compared with national growth of 5.2 per cent.
He said the budget’s theme, “Bringing the Vision Closer to the People and Forging a Legacy”, should translate into tangible benefits that would make life easier for the public, adding that the state should not risk losing public support by prioritising its legacy over people’s needs.
Lim also welcomed the appointment of new state secretary Datuk Dr Jafri Abdul Jalil, effective August 3, 2026, and thanked his predecessor Datuk Seri Zulkifli Long for his service.
Lim said ordinary people and micro, small and medium enterprises were facing challenging economic conditions and should not have to contend with higher taxes and compliance costs, pointing to land tax collections rising from RM116 million in both 2024 and 2025 to RM165 million as at September this year, an increase of RM49 million in nine months despite the payment deadline being extended to the end of 2026; he also cited national GDP growth of six per cent in the second quarter of 2026 and a 13.5 per cent increase in the banking sector’s pre-tax profits, from RM48.3 billion in 2024 to RM54.8 billion in 2025.
He also called on the state government to provide the remaining RM500,000 for road widening and safety improvements at Pintas Berani 5 near SJK(C) Kwang Hwa in Bagan Jermal, saying the RM1 million approved by Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming would widen the road from one lane to two and that the additional allocation was needed to improve safety for the school’s 1,118 pupils, teachers and other road users; he said the state only needed to contribute half the project’s remaining cost and that the funds had already been channelled to the Seberang Perai City Council.
On water supply, Lim urged the state government to table its bulk water supply agreement with Perak’s Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd in the state assembly for debate and approval, saying the 40-year arrangement from 2032 carried an estimated cost of RM24.6 billion up to 2072, comprising RM8.4 billion in infrastructure capacity charges and RM16.2 billion in water supply charges; he said the agreement should be made public and that the state should seek Perak’s consent to disclose its terms even if a non-disclosure agreement was in place, as Penang residents would ultimately bear the cost.
Lim also proposed an independent state commission of inquiry into the October 25 slope collapse at Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, which killed 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin and led to the immediate evacuation of six nearby homes, saying those responsible should be held accountable; he disputed claims that the project had been approved during his tenure as chief minister from 2008 to 2018, stating that planning permission was granted in 2023 and earthworks and building plans in 2024, when he was no longer chief minister or finance minister, and said the allegations had been circulated on eight websites and referred to his lawyer for legal action.
Turning to the proposed 70-acre reclamation project off Persiaran Karpal Singh, estimated to cost RM1 billion, and the agreement to rehabilitate the 84-acre Jelutong landfill, Lim questioned why the agreement had not been cancelled after the contractor’s applications were rejected five times by the Department of Environment, despite an October 18 deadline set by the chief minister; he also asked why extensions had been granted for more than six years since the agreement was signed on February 21, 2020, how much the contractor still owed the Penang Development Corporation and state government, and why the reclamation project was proceeding without a signed agreement.
Citing the Auditor-General’s Report 2026, Lim criticised the Penang Development Corporation’s handling of the Jalan Perusahaan-Jalan Tok Kangar road and bridge upgrading project, saying the combined cost of RM63.4 million for its two phases — RM10.6 million for Phase 1 and RM52.8 million for Phase 2 — was RM20.4 million, or 47 per cent, above the original RM43 million estimate; he said the audit found that Phase 2 had taken more than seven years after its open tender was awarded on July 12, 2019, that delays reached 2,278 days and that RM3.12 million in progress payments had been made to a replacement contractor before a formal contract was signed, while PDC had still received a six-month bonus for 2024, paid in February 2025.
He also questioned PDC’s ability to undertake the proposed 1,142-acre Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 development, of which 872 acres would be available for investors, asking whether the project should instead be opened to private-sector participation; Lim cited the sale of 559 acres of PDC land at Byram, Batu Kawan, for RM646 million through a direct deal without an open tender, compared with a subsequent open request for proposal offering RM818 million, or RM172 million more, and argued that a private-sector partnership could bring in funds sooner and accelerate development.
On economic prospects, Lim said Penang and Malaysia had benefited from geopolitical and economic tensions between the United States and China, as well as the impact of US President Donald Trump’s tariffs, with foreign investment and exports reaching record levels, particularly in electronics; he welcomed the federal government’s RM100 million allocation approved by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for the Penang Technology Financial Centre, which he said could build on the state’s technological strengths in digital development, artificial intelligence and new forms of trade.
However, Lim said economic growth was uneven and some sectors continued to face difficulties, calling for a separate Special Financial Zone to attract foreign funds and activities involving cryptocurrency, fintech and digital finance, which he said fell outside the Penang Technology Financial Centre’s focus on technology, start-ups and AI; he proposed a 40-hectare site at Ampang Jajar between the Bagan and Permatang Pauh parliamentary constituencies, near public transport links including the planned LRT station at Penang Sentral, expected to be completed in 2032, saying this would help balance development between Penang island and Seberang Perai.

Title: Penang studies Third Link bridge as alternative to undersea tunnel, will seek port commission feedback
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 2 — The state government is still conducting a conceptual design study for the proposed Penang Third Link Bridge as an alternative to the undersea tunnel, before presenting it to the Penang Port Commission (PPC) for feedback.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the state government had approved a realignment study based on a bridge design concept, taking into consideration plans to expand Penang Port and the need to ease traffic congestion in Gurney Bay and its surrounding areas.
He said the proposed realignment involved shifting the route northwards to ensure it was compatible with Penang Port's expansion plans, while avoiding any disruption to port operations and vessel navigation routes.
“At present, the conceptual design study is underway, and its findings will be presented to the PPC for feedback and further consideration.
“This assessment aims to ensure that any decision on the project's implementation takes into account technical feasibility, financial implications, people's mobility needs, shipping safety and marine navigation, as well as the long-term benefits to the state's socioeconomic development,” he said.
He said this in response to a question from Teh Lai Heng (PH-Komtar) on the latest status, as of September 2026, of the three highway projects and one undersea tunnel project, during the state assembly sitting here today.
The proposed 6.5-kilometre undersea tunnel linking Gurney Drive to Bagan Ajam on the mainland is part of the Penang Transport Master Plan (PTMP).
On the North Coastal Paired Road (NCPR) project, Zairil said the state government was reviewing part of the proposed alignment, covering the route from Tanjung Bungah to Teluk Bahang, to ensure that it took into account technical suitability, local sensitivities, population density and the risk of soil erosion.
In this regard, he said the terms of the Sub-Agreement (SA) were being finalised before it could be signed.
“At the same time, the state government is also undertaking an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for part of the new alignment to ensure that the proposed development takes into account transportation needs, safety and the interests of local residents,” he said.
The NCPR project is part of a package involving three major roads and a tunnel, which was awarded in 2013. It involves the construction of a 10.61-kilometre highway, comprising an 8.41-kilometre land route and a 2.2-kilometre coastal viaduct linking Tanjung Bungah and Teluk Bahang.
Construction is expected to begin in 2026 and be completed by 2031. Upon completion, travel time between Tanjung Bungah and Teluk Bahang is expected to be reduced from 30 to 45 minutes during peak hours to just seven minutes. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan spent RM10.86m on house repair aid for the poor in 2024 and 2025, says MB
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 2 — The Kelantan government allocated more than RM10.86 million for house repair works and the provision of building materials to poor and underprivileged households in the state in 2024 and 2025.
Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud said a total of 1,034 assistance packages were provided during the period under the Dhuafa’ Housing Assistance programme implemented by the Kelantan State Development Office.
He said of the total, 473 assistance packages were provided in 2024, involving an expenditure of RM5.04 million, while 561 were channelled in 2025, involving an allocation of RM5.811 million.
“The assistance covers house repair works and the provision of building materials, based on the needs and extent of damage to the homes of eligible recipients,” he said.
He said this in reply to a question from Mohd Azmawi Fikri Abdul Ghani (BN-Nenggiri) during the state assembly sitting at the Kota Darulnaim Complex here today.
Elaborating further, Mohd Nassuruddin said the selection of aid recipients was carried out through an application, investigation and verification process by the Land and District offices, subject to eligibility requirements and the availability of funds.
In addition to house repair assistance and contributions of building materials, the state government also provides 180 new houses annually throughout Kelantan under the same programme.
“Each house is valued at RM65,000, with a total allocation of approximately RM11.7 million annually. Insya-Allah, we will be able to assist more people in need,” he said. — Bernama
